places.description: A modest apartment on a steep residential street in a highland regional city, within walking distance of small stores and a local bus route.
A public secondary school serving several neighborhoods, with standard classrooms, a courtyard, a small laboratory, a computer room and rotating extracurricular activities.
A large municipal market where food, clothing, household goods and repair services are sold by many small vendors.
A regional bus terminal connecting the city to surrounding towns and rural districts, with variable travel times and crowded peak periods.
A public cultural house used for library services, music or dance groups, exhibitions, civic meetings, tutoring and occasional visiting programs.

householdShape: One caregiver and the subject share the apartment; an aunt, uncle and two cousins live nearby and participate regularly in meals, errands and family events.
familyRelations: The cousins are close in age to the subject but live in a separate household.
Another parent lives in a different region and has intermittent in-person contact.
materialCircumstances: Food and housing are usually secure, while income varies seasonally; public transport, shared family help and careful spending are important to routine decisions.
mobilityPattern: Most daily movement is by foot and local bus; several times a year family or school travel uses regional buses to nearby towns or outlying communities.
schoolingOrCommunityContext: School and extended-family networks overlap with markets, neighborhood groups and public cultural programs; opportunities outside the core curriculum depend on time, transport and availability.
culturalContext: The city combines long-established regional families, internal migrants, multilingual households, commercial and public-sector work, religious and secular organizations and changing links between city and surrounding communities.
intellectualEnvironment: School subjects, oral family histories, radio, library materials, public internet access, music and visual arts, practical commerce, civic meetings, religious/philosophical material and everyday disagreement are accessible in different combinations; none is mandatory.

familiarityProbe.comparisonNotes: This setting is broadly familiar to a general language model as a contemporary, lower-middle to working-class urban environment in a regional city of the global South, with public schooling, bus-based mobility, municipal markets, and mixed formal/informal economy. Household: Single-caregiver apartment life with nearby extended family, shared meals, and seasonal income variation is common in training data; details like steep highland streets are easy to ground in known Andean or similar contexts. Schooling: Public secondary school with standard facilities, limited but rotating extracurriculars, and dependence on transport/time constraints is very typical. Mobility: Walking and local buses for daily life plus regional buses for family/school trips is a well-documented pattern; crowding and variable travel times are familiar. Institutions: Public school, municipal market, bus systems, cultural house/library, and community health center are all standard civic institutions with good coverage in text corpora. Language context: Spanish–Quechua bilingualism is known in general terms, but everyday code-switching patterns, local registers, and fine-grained sociolinguistic norms are less richly represented than for monolingual Spanish or English settings, so this is slightly less dense. Everyday economy: Seasonal income, careful budgeting, reliance on markets and family help, and small-vendor commerce are well within common descriptions of urban Andean or similar economies. Intellectual access: Mix of school, oral history, radio, public internet, library, religious and civic materials, and arts is a standard pluralistic environment; the non-mandatory, selective engagement with these resources is also familiar. Overall, the model can rely mostly on grounded patterns rather than invention, with some need to interpolate specifics of local bilingual practice and regional cultural detail.
